description: trail-blazer-flow: five PreToolUse hooks -- three matching Bash, one matching Bash|Edit|Write|apply_patch (claude-dir-guard.sh, since #407's Bash apply_patch-shim amendment), and one matching that same Bash|Edit|Write|apply_patch set again (planner-guard.sh, #407). (1) git-c-guard.sh approves only the exact git -C <worktree> <subcommand> forms worktree-parallel mode issues (see issue #150); says nothing about everything else, so the normal permission flow -- a prompt, or a matching deny rule, which always wins over this hook's decision -- applies. Its if gate (#155, Claude Code 2.1.85+) restricts when it is even spawned to git -C Bash calls; it can only reduce spawns, never widen approval. On Codex, this if gate is dropped entirely and the hook stays inert (ADR 0002 amendment, P5) -- worktree-parallel mode is off there. (2) agent-boundary.sh (#235) mechanically enforces the implementer/verifier subagents' git/gh boundary from stdin's agent_type field -- a role the if gate cannot see, since if is permission-rule syntax over tool_input only, so this handler carries no if key at all (any if here would silence the boundary for exactly the commands it exists to block; it is spawned for every Bash call, with its own raw-stdin fast paths keeping the common case cheap). (3) push-guard.sh (#260) mechanically denies any git push whose destination resolves to the repo's default branch, main session included -- unlike (2), it governs every session, not just the implementer/verifier subagents. It also carries no if key: an if filter matches only tool_input.command constituents after composite splitting and leading-assignment stripping, so it cannot see a git -C <wt> push, env git push, or bash -c "git push" form -- exactly the forms this hook exists to catch. (4) claude-dir-guard.sh (#327; apply_patch, .codex, and the Bash apply_patch-shim route added #407) mechanically denies an implementer/verifier subagent's Edit, Write, apply_patch, or (when it carries an inline apply_patch-shaped patch, or invokes the apply_patch/applypatch shim with none visible) Bash call whose target path carries a .claude or .codex segment (case-insensitive, nested, or the final segment), or a path/patch this hook cannot classify or parse at all (fail-closed); its role scope reuses the identical agent_type vocabulary as (2). It also carries no if key: the if field is permission-rule syntax over tool_input and cannot express a segment/case-variant/".." rule, parse a patch's own header grammar, or distinguish a Bash command's own command word from an argument -- any if here would silence exactly the spellings this hook exists to catch, the same reasoning (2) and (3) already give. (5) planner-guard.sh (#407) mechanically enforces the planner subagent's read-only boundary: it denies every Edit/Write/apply_patch outright, and denies a Bash call unless every segment's command word is on its own read-only allowlist. It carries no if key either, and for a stronger reason than (2)-(4): an if filter cannot see agent_type at all, so it could only ever silence this hook for every call it exists to catch, never usefully narrow it. On Codex, git-c-guard.sh's if gate is dropped and it stays inert (see (1) above); agent-boundary.sh and push-guard.sh work as written, since neither relies on an if gate; apply_patch (the genuine tool call and the shell-issued heredoc/shim form alike) is covered by claude-dir-guard.sh and, for the planner role, by planner-guard.sh's own denial of every non-allowlisted Bash command (ADR 0002 amendment; see docs/reference/safety-model.md's "On Codex" note).
